## Summary

Inspect post-accept learning write-back triggers for a feature, or book the review.

## Usage

```bash
amber learnings --target <repo> [--feature <id>] [--reviewed --owner <id>] [--surface <path>] [--json]
```

## Execution Contract

<CommandBlock
  context="Target Repository"
  nature="idempotent-write"
  command="amber learnings --target path/to/repo"
/>

## Command Details

```text
Inspect post-accept learning write-back triggers for a feature, or book the review.
Read-only inspection by default; --reviewed books the review on the feature entry.

Options:
  --feature <id>     Feature to inspect (defaults to the current lifecycle focus).
  --reviewed         Book the learning review (requires --feature; overwrites any prior booking).
  --owner <id>       Durable Amber surface that owns the learned behavior; exactly one is required when booking.
                     Canonical owner routes:
                       - skill: Will the durable behavior primarily teach an agent how to perform a specific task? Owns instruction documents that guide an agent through a specific task; it does not execute the task.
                       - hook: Must this behavior be checked at a lifecycle boundary every time that boundary is reached? Owns deterministic lifecycle reminders, blockers, records, or policy checks at a host boundary.
                       - command: Is the durable behavior best exposed as a short, fixed operator entry point? Owns a concise, explicit CLI or manual entry point that invokes a stable operation.
                       - standard: Is the behavior a reusable set of review checks applied across changes? Owns reusable review criteria and check collections; it does not itself run a scheduler.
                       - script: Is the behavior a deterministic extraction, validation, transformation, or formatting helper? Owns deterministic support logic for extracting, validating, transforming, or formatting data.
                       - workflow-pack: Should the behavior be carried as a declarative bundle of reusable governance pieces? Owns declarative bundles that compose skills, standards, scripts, and approval gates without autonomous execution.
                       - loop-contract: Does the behavior define recurring-work trigger, cadence, state, stop, and review semantics? Owns declarative repeated-work contracts for trigger, cadence, state spine, hard stops, and review gates; it is not a scheduler.
                       - ci: Must the check run on a protected repository event or pull-request gate? Owns continuous checks that actually run on protected repository or PR events; it does not imply general target-project execution.
  --surface <path>   Knowledge surface the review was written to. Repeatable;
                     a single flag also accepts a comma-separated list.
  --json             Emit the machine-readable envelope.

Boundary: Amber detects and reminds; it never writes knowledge docs itself.

Examples:
  amber learnings --target .
  amber learnings --target . --feature F001
  amber learnings --target . --feature F001 --reviewed --owner command --surface docs/specs/f001.md
```

## Boundaries & Safety

- `--target <path>` selects repository state. Amber confines these target-relative paths, refusing `..` and symlink escapes before reading or writing: plan and scaffold destinations (including `accept --plan`), memory and context payloads, harness inputs, adapter allow-lists, workflow reports and their output directory, ledger exports, execution readiness plans, session and worktree state, governance report output, wiki export and handoff bundle output directories.
- Path validation is not OS sandboxing, and the confinement above covers only the surfaces it names, and a confined flag still accepts an absolute destination only when it stays inside the target. `governance audit --output`, `governance readiness --output`, `security audit --output`, `loop record --output`, and `explain --markdown` resolve against the working directory instead of `--target`. A path flag not listed here is confined only when the command that reads it routes through the boundary. A governed or verification command still runs with your user's file permissions.
- `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess` and `governance report` reject output destinations that resolve to the target root, including `.`, an absolute root path, `nested/..`, and symlink or junction aliases of the root. Output subdirectories and defaults are unchanged.
- `wiki export` and `handoff bundle` check all planned file destinations and their parent directories before the first write, including copied wiki pages and optional replay files. An existing child symlink or junction outside the target refuses the export without changing output files. `wiki export` also checks every page it copies, so a page that shares its bytes with another name refuses the export before anything is written, including when both names stay inside the target. Concurrent link replacement is not prevented.
- A planned output file that shares its bytes with another name — a hard link, or a link to one — is refused before the write by `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess --output-dir`, `governance report --output`, `ledger export --out`, `knowledge context-review-sample --output`, `gate --plan` and `accept --plan` (the plan file they edit in place), `handoff` (the `session-handoff.md` it overwrites), `hooks install` (the `pre-commit` hook and its `.amber-backup` it overwrites), `knowledge plan propose` (the plan file it overwrites when `--force`) and `sync --execute` / scaffold refresh (the controlled template files it overwrites and their `.bak` copies) — and `amber context benchmark` applies the same refusal to the benchmark reports it persists — even when both names stay inside the target. A link to a single in-target file is still written through, so it replaces that file's bytes; `workflow assess` is the exception, because it confines its output file to the `--output-dir` and so refuses a link whose referent sits elsewhere in the target. Like the child-link check above, this is checked before the write, so a link swapped in during the write is not caught.
- `handoff validate --bundle-dir .` and `workflow assess --handoff-bundle-dir .` still accept root-level bundles as read-only inputs. Explicit handoff validation paths outside `--target` are refused.
- Writing governance state goes through two shared helpers — the in-place JSON writer and the append-only JSONL ledger append — and both refuse a leaf that shares its bytes with another name. That covers the `.amber/` writers built on them (context pages and Loadouts, audit and event ledgers) without each one repeating the check; a raw write outside those helpers is guarded only where its own surface names it above.
- **Fail-Closed Behavior**: Corrupt governance state or invalid schema parameters immediately halt execution with non-zero exit codes.
